claims.content: The Customer wants to browse and search auction inventory items by filtering based on criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location, Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, and Cost Range (which may be combined) to narrow the product list.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer wants to browse and search auction inventory items by filtering based on criteria such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location, Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, and Cost Range (which may be combined) to narrow the product list.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer accesses the browse/search function, selects or combines one or more product filters or search criteria (e.g., Product Type or Retail Category), and receives a list of matching auction inventory items.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The use case starts when the Customer initiates browsing or searching of the auction inventory.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The use case ends when the Customer obtains a filtered or searched list of products matching the selected criteria.
in_scope_actions: Searching for products using search criteria

claims.content: Customer
Auction inventory data is populated and available in the system for the Auctioneer to access.
Products are marked as both 'Auction Available' and 'Auction Eligible' in the JTV enterprise systems so they are counted in the inventory numbers.

The Customer initiates the search by entering a Product ID or Customer Email Address and clicking 'Go', or by selecting one or more search parameters (e.g., Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, Product Type, Cost Range) and clicking 'Find Product'.
The Customer uses the Endeca or Endeca-like search and navigation capability to browse the auction inventory.

The Customer selects or combines one or more product filters or search criteria, such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Type, Brand, Location, Product ID, Customer Email Address, Schedule Date range, Auction Duration, and Cost Range, to narrow the product list.

The Customer initiates the search by clicking the 'Go' button after entering a Product ID or Customer Email Address, or by clicking the 'Find Product' button after selecting or combining search parameters.

The system displays a table titled 'Search Results' containing columns for Action, Image, Product ID, Auction #, Description, Open Bid, High Bid, Unit Cost, Starts, Ends, Duration, Product Type, and Increment, with rows showing matching auction items, each with thumbnail images, bid values, start/end times, duration, and increment amount.

Diverges from Step 1: instead of using the Endeca search and navigation capability directly, the Customer accesses the browse/search capability via a Site Map page that lists available Categories, Product Types, and Gemstone Types as direct links to specific pages or Endeca results pages.

Diverges from Step 1: the Customer enters product browsing through SEO-optimized landing pages focused on specific gemstone or product types, which contain direct links to relevant filtered product categories such as 'all loose tanzanite stones' or 'all tanzanite rings'.
Diverges from Step 2: the Customer selects radio button options to choose between viewing 'Items currently online only' or 'All sellable auction inventory'.

Diverges from Step 2: the Customer uses combinable radio buttons to view items with or without images and/or with or without a valid sellable inventory location, altering the composition of the result set.
Diverges from Step 4: the Customer switches the product results between 'List View' and 'Catalog View' display modes.
Diverges from Step 4: the Customer sorts the product results by 'Current Price: low to high' using a dropdown menu.
Diverges from Step 4: the Customer groups the results using a scrolling list box and selecting a grouping option such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material, or Brand.

missing_aspects: The claim's mention of selecting a 'scope radio button' is supported by the evidence describing 'Radio button options', but the evidence does not explicitly define these buttons as setting a 'search scope'; it defines them as criteria for the report view.

The claim states that this action 'generates corresponding columns in the Results section.' While the evidence confirms that user choices from the Grouping list box generate columns, it lists 'Any columns generated...' separately from the fixed columns. The claim implies a direct 1-to-1 generation of columns for the selected option which may be an over-specification compared to the evidence's phrasing of 'Any columns generated by user choices'.

claims.content: Diverges from Step 1: If the Customer clicks a link that contains no product, the system serves a 'No Results Found' page.

Diverges from Step 4: If the search results contain no matching products, the system displays a 'No Results Found' page instead of the Search Results table. The page includes (1) an apology message stating no matches were found, (2) a 'Search Tips' section with five suggestions (check typos, remove unnecessary words, try plural/singular forms, use fewer/generic keywords, contact support), and (3) a 'May We Suggest'/'Popular Searches' section with static lists of popular gemstone and jewelry searches plus dynamically updated search terms/phrases using Omniture data.

Diverges from Step 4: The system prevents any product without an available image from appearing in search results or catalog pages, so items lacking images are omitted from the displayed results; if all matching products lack images, the result set can be empty even though the search criteria matched inventory items.

missing_aspects: Explicit recovery or exit path after the No Results Found page is displayed (e.g., return to search, modify filters, or terminate the use case)
Explicit confirmation that the displayed content is triggered by 'zero matching products' specifically, rather than just a generic 'no matches' or empty query condition.

claims.content: After the Customer initiates a search, the system displays a table titled Search Results using the default column order: Action (checkbox), Item thumbnail image, Product ID (SKU #) with link to the SKU History page, Auction ID number, Description, Opening Bid, High Bid, Item Unit Cost, Start time (initially blank), End time (initially blank), Duration (initially blank), Product Type, and Increment; the rows show matching auction inventory items with thumbnail images, bid values, and increment amount.

When the successful search was by Product ID, the system displays a Search Results for Item section containing a table with columns Auction Status, Auction_Seq, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve, High Bid, # of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder, populated with rows corresponding to the matching auction history.

When the results are displayed in catalog/product-module format, each filtered product item is represented by a Product Module containing a thumbnail image, a short description (On-Air Description), a countdown timer in D:HH:MM:SS format showing time remaining, the current high bid, and a QuickBid button.
If the Customer groups the results, the Results section includes columns generated by the selected grouping option in addition to the fixed result columns.

missing_aspects: The cited evidence supports the display of the table and its contents but does not explicitly state that this specific view is triggered exclusively 'by Product ID' or distinguish it from other search types.
The cited evidence describes the components of the Product Module but does not explicitly link this display format to the outcome of a 'search' action as implied by the claim context.
